notes:
BLOCKED on HELPER_MISSING before driver implementation: the pinned upstream is a Unity TurtleBot3 simulation whose only ROS motion input is an unacknowledged Twist subscription, and the source offers no ROS-callable independent stop or safe-state service/action. Nav2SLAMExampleProject/Assets/Scripts/AGVController.cs:41 subscribes TwistMsg on cmd_vel; :44-49 only stores linear.x, angular.z and the receive time; :26 declares ROSTimeout = 0.5 s and :122-127 zero the cached velocities when a command is late. That is a publisher-side timeout with no reply, not an acknowledged stop, and the RosDriver contract rejects zero-velocity publication as a stop binding. The only other ROS surface is observational: LaserScanSensor.cs:40,103 publishes LaserScan on the prefab's /scan (Nav2SLAMExampleProject/Assets/Prefabs/TurtleBot3ManualConfig.prefab:486), ROSClockPublisher.cs:55 publishes Clock on clock, and ROSTransformTreePublisher.cs:44 publishes TFMessage on /tf. No RegisterService or RegisterUnityService call exists in the Unity scripts; ros2_docker/colcon_ws/src/ROS-TCP-Endpoint/ros_tcp_endpoint/server.py:241-302 can register a service only when the Unity client asks for one, and this project never does. The project's own stop route is manual: readmes/run_example.md:75 says to press Play twice in Unity to stop and restart the simulation. A RosDriver fake could replay the observations or echo a cmd_vel publication, but it cannot supply a native acknowledged stop: safety_bindings on RosDriver accept only input-free service/action bindings, safe_state.achieved_by cannot be a publication, and a fake service that does not exist upstream would fail G7 and would fabricate the safety guarantee. A direct Driver does not help: the Unity side is C# and the ROS-TCP-Endpoint bridge is not rosbridge and exposes no stop endpoint; there is no Python device class to wrap. The simulated TurtleBot is a mobile base, so the honest risk is at least R2, not the card's R0 floor; at R2 an independent stop is required and this upstream has none. Scope not covered by any package: no driver.py, fake.py, driver.lock.json, reference.json, REFERENCE.md or test_driver.py was written because a pass would require either observation-only metadata or an invented stop. Diagnostic gate (only run, 1 of the 6 allowed) failed G1 G2 G3 G9: G1 missing driver.py, driver.lock.json and test_driver.py (RESULT.json was written after this run); G2 no lock; G3 import; G9 missing tests. No upstream code was imported or executed, no node, Unity editor, ROS graph, simulator or hardware was run, no network or pip install was used, and the clone was not modified. No human signature exists and reviewed_by remains null because no lock was written.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block against the pin: AGVController subscribes cmd_vel as Twist (Nav2SLAMExampleProject/Assets/Scripts/AGVController.cs:41), its callback only stores linear.x, angular.z and the receive time (44-49), and ROSUpdate zeroes the cached velocities after the 0.5 s ROSTimeout (26, 122-127) without any reply; the other ROS surfaces only publish /scan, clock and /tf (LaserScanSensor.cs:40 and 103, ROSClockPublisher.cs:55, ROSTransformTreePublisher.cs:44), and no Unity script registers a ROS service, so there is no acknowledged stop for RosDriver to bind and HELPER_MISSING follows the mvsim precedent. Every citation in the notes matches its line. One correction to the notes: a Unity-simulated TurtleBot3 is R0 (simulated state, MHS/spec/04-safety.md:66-76), not 'at least R2', which applies to a hardware mobile base. The reviewer changed no authored file; the gate re-run rewrote check-report.json with the same findings. For the human reviewer: Unity steps its physics on its own clock and nothing in the ROS graph pauses or stops it; the documented stop is pressing Play in the Unity editor (readmes/run_example.md:75). ROS reaches Unity only through ROS-TCP-Endpoint, not rosbridge, so a RosDriver deployment also needs rosbridge on the same ROS 2 graph.
